newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end at highs, get Wall St boost.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end at highs, get Wall St boost.

text.p: South African shares got a late shot in the arm from a strong Wall Street to give life to a market that on Monday was still suffering a hangover from disappointing reserve figures, dealers said.
A lacklustre session, that saw healthy volumes but little price movement, finally shook off the gloom to finish at its day highs as Wall Street powered forward on its bull run.
"Wall Street opened and the market just went that bit higher just before the end," one dealer said.

The overall index finished at 7,036.3, up 15.7 points, as the industrials pulled ahead by 23.3 points to end at 8,245.7. Golds fell 5.9 points to 1,727 as concerns over the weakening bullion price dogged the index.
The day saw some overseas interest, but not much. "There were some foreigners in there, but it was mainly local buying," a dealer said.
Dealers reflected that the day had been a quiet one depressed by Friday's negative September reserves figures which saw the Reserve Bank using 612 million rand in foreign credit lines.
